question: Once the RFC structure is repaired, should OpenClaw accept the one-package/one-new-agent Claws contract and require the experimental implementation stack to conform to it?
rationale: Repository policy determines the acceptance process, but it cannot decide whether this new cross-surface CLI, schema, ownership, lifecycle, and compatibility contract should become OpenClaw product policy.

options.title: Accept and restack
options.body: Approve the complete-agent contract behind the experimental gate, create the implementation issue, update the RFC metadata, and require the linked stack to meet the acceptance criteria.

options.title: Continue incubation
options.body: Keep the RFC in draft while maintainers narrow or resolve the remaining version-one, migration, and shared-schema questions.

options.title: Decline first-class Claws
options.body: Do not establish a unified Claw lifecycle and retain composition through existing skill, plugin, and operator-managed configuration surfaces.

recommendation.title: Accept and restack
recommendation.body: Approve the complete-agent contract behind the experimental gate, create the implementation issue, update the RFC metadata, and require the linked stack to meet the acceptance criteria.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the repository's RFC process and are the strongest history-backed routing owner for the acceptance decision.
